--- .env.example	
+++ .env.example	
@@ -1,700 +1,700 @@
 # Nexus Proxy — environment configuration
 #
 # Copy this file to `.env` (which is gitignored) and fill in real values.
 # Every variable has a sane default for local dev with Ollama, so you can
 # leave most unset while you iterate.
 
 # --- Hot-reloadable knobs (issue #491) ---------------------------------------
 # Sending SIGHUP to the nexus process re-reads exactly these env vars
 # without a full restart (see ReloadHotReloadable in internal/config/config.go):
 #   NEXUS_LOG_LEVEL        # hot-reloadable via SIGHUP
 #   NEXUS_LOG_FORMAT       # hot-reloadable via SIGHUP
 #   NEXUS_DEBUG            # hot-reloadable via SIGHUP
 #   NEXUS_RATE_LIMIT_RPM   # hot-reloadable via SIGHUP
 #   NEXUS_RATE_LIMIT_BURST # hot-reloadable via SIGHUP
 # Every other var requires a full process restart to take effect.
 
 # --- Config file (issue #424) -----------------------------------------------
 # Optional path to a YAML config file. Env vars always take precedence over
 # file values. When unset, Load() searches ./config.yaml then ~/.nexus/config.yaml.
 # Set to /dev/null (or any non-existent path) to force env-var-only mode.
 NEXUS_CONFIG_FILE=
 
 # --- HTTP server ----------------------------------------------------------
 NEXUS_ADDR=:8000
 # Listener-side timeouts and header cap (issue #77). These bound the inbound
 # HTTP connection so slow-header/slow-body abuse and oversized headers cannot
 # exhaust the server. Distinct from the outbound NEXUS_HTTP_* transport knobs
 # which control upstream client calls.
 # Full request read deadline (headers + body). 0 disables.
 NEXUS_SERVER_READ_TIMEOUT=30s
 # Full response write deadline. 0 (disabled) is the streaming-safe default —
 # SSE streaming responses can run for minutes and a non-zero write timeout
 # would kill them mid-stream. Set only when behind a buffering reverse proxy.
 NEXUS_SERVER_WRITE_TIMEOUT=0
 # Keep-alive idle wait between requests on a persistent connection. 0 disables.
 NEXUS_SERVER_IDLE_TIMEOUT=120s
 # Maximum total size of HTTP request headers in bytes. 0 uses the Go default
 # (1 MiB).
 NEXUS_SERVER_MAX_HEADER_BYTES=1048576
 # Hard cap on the total request-body size in bytes (issue #11). The chat
 # handler wraps r.Body with http.MaxBytesReader so an oversized POST is
 # rejected with 413 before any allocation happens. 0 or negative falls back
 # to the default (1 MiB). Raise it if you proxy very large chat payloads.
 NEXUS_MAX_BODY_BYTES=1048576
 # MaxResponseBytes caps upstream response bodies read into memory (issue #365).
 # A malicious upstream returning gigabytes could otherwise cause uncontrolled
 # memory growth. Default 64 MiB accommodates large frontier completions;
 # raise it if you expect very long responses.
 NEXUS_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES=67108864
 # CascadeMaxResponseBytes caps cascade response bodies (issue #742).
 # Independent from NEXUS_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES so operators can tune cascade
 # bounds separately. Default 64 MiB.
 NEXUS_CASCADE_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES=67108864
 # Graceful shutdown drain window (issue #121). Upper bound on how long the
 # server waits for in-flight requests to complete after SIGTERM/SIGINT before
 # forcibly closing connections. The prior hardcoded 10s truncated frontier
 # SSE streams mid-token and cut off fusion arbiter calls that had just opened
 # their 60s timeout window. Default 30s accommodates a long frontier stream
 # while staying under a typical K8s terminationGracePeriodSeconds of 30s.
 # 0 falls back to the default (it does NOT disable the drain). Negative is
 # rejected at boot. A value shorter than NEXUS_SERVER_READ_TIMEOUT emits a
 # boot warning since in-flight uploads could be truncated mid-read. Operators
 # running frontier streams of 120s+ should raise this and set their pod's
 # terminationGracePeriodSeconds accordingly.
 NEXUS_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT=30s
 # Effective inbound TLS posture (issue #444). When true, the security-headers
 # middleware stamps `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` on every
 # response so clients pin HTTPS and refuse plaintext fallbacks. When false
 # (default), HSTS is omitted — emitting it over plaintext is a spec
 # violation. Set this to true when:
 #   * the proxy terminates TLS directly (inbound https://, see issue #39), OR
 #   * the proxy sits BEHIND a TLS-terminating reverse proxy (nginx, Caddy,
 #     ELB, Cloudflare). The proxy only sees plaintext but the outer hop is
 #     HTTPS, so HSTS is still safe to advertise.
 # The proxy does NOT verify the inbound scheme automatically; this knob is
 # the single source of truth so an operator behind a TLS proxy gets HSTS
 # without the proxy having to inspect X-Forwarded-Proto.
 NEXUS_TLS_ENABLED=false
 
 # --- HTTP transport tuning (internal/transport/transport.go) -------------
 # Shared pooled http.Client for all outbound upstream calls (Ollama,
 # frontier API, arbiter synthesis). Tune these when the proxy is driving
 # many concurrent upstreams and you want to bound TCP overhead or avoid
 # hitting upstream connection limits.
 # Max idle connections maintained per upstream host (default 100). A host
 # is a "host:port" pair, so hitting the same Ollama instance reuses warm
 # connections. Set to 0 to fall back to Go's default.
 NEXUS_HTTP_MAX_IDLE_CONNS_PER_HOST=100
 # Max total connections per upstream host. 0 = unlimited (default).
 # Set this if your Ollama or frontier API enforces a per-host connection
 # ceiling and you want the client-side pool to respect it proactively.
 NEXUS_HTTP_MAX_CONNS_PER_HOST=0
 # Maximum time an idle connection sits idle before being closed (default 90s).
 NEXUS_HTTP_IDLE_CONN_TIMEOUT=90s
 # Maximum time a TCP dial may take (default 30s). Set higher if your
 # network is slow or Ollama is on a distant host.
 NEXUS_HTTP_DIAL_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT=30s
 # Maximum time waiting for response headers after fully sending the request
 # (default 30s). Guards against slow upstream servers that hold the
 # connection open but send body data very slowly.
 NEXUS_HTTP_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT=30s
 # Path to a PEM file containing the client certificate for mTLS. Set both
 # this AND NEXUS_HTTP_CLIENT_KEY_FILE to enable client-cert auth against
 # the upstream (Ollama, frontier, arbiter). Leave empty to disable.
 NEXUS_HTTP_CLIENT_CERT_FILE=
 # Path to a PEM file containing the client private key for mTLS.
 # Required when NEXUS_HTTP_CLIENT_CERT_FILE is set.
 NEXUS_HTTP_CLIENT_KEY_FILE=
 # Path to a PEM CA certificate used to verify the upstream server cert.
 # When set, the server certificate must be signed by this CA. Leave empty
 # to use the system certificate pool (default).
 NEXUS_HTTP_CA_FILE=
 
 # --- Structured logging (issue #3) ---------------------------------------
 # Minimum level for the structured stderr logger.
 # One of: debug | info | warn | error. Default: info.
 NEXUS_LOG_LEVEL=info  # hot-reloadable via SIGHUP
 # Wire format for the structured stderr logger.
 # One of: json | text. Default: json (set "text" for a friendlier local view).
 NEXUS_LOG_FORMAT=json  # hot-reloadable via SIGHUP
 
 # --- Debug request/response tracing (issue #33) -------------------------
 # When true, the chat handler emits a structured trace for every
 # proxied request covering: inbound summary, middleware transforms
 # (RAG / TOON / meta-prompt), routing decision + reason, upstream
 # target host, and a truncated response preview. Default: false.
 # Production has zero overhead when this is off. API keys are always
 # redacted (masked to last 4 chars); Authorization headers are stripped
 # from any captured payload. Distinct from NEXUS_LOG_LEVEL=debug: this
 # flag specifically adds payload-level visibility gated independently.
 NEXUS_DEBUG=false  # hot-reloadable via SIGHUP
 # Cap on the response-body preview the debug trace logs. Larger values
 # surface more of the upstream reply but make the log line bigger.
 # Default: 512 bytes.
 NEXUS_DEBUG_BODY_BYTES=512
 
 # --- Distributed tracing (issue #41, #122) ------------------------------
 # When set, an OTLP/JSON trace exporter is started and registered as the
 # process-wide tracer. Spans are buffered in a bounded channel and POSTed
 # asynchronously; dropped spans are counted and surfaced on /metrics as
 # nexus_tracing_dropped_total. Leave empty to disable tracing (default).
 NEXUS_TRACING_ENDPOINT=
 # Timeout for each POST to the OTLP collector (issue #804). High-latency
 # collectors (multi-region aggregators, TLS handshake delay) may need more
 # than the conservative 10s default.
 NEXUS_TRACING_TIMEOUT=10s
 
 # OTLP retry/back-off parameters (issue #803). The back-off follows
 # exponential growth: base * 2^(attempt-1) capped at max.
 # Maximum retry attempts after the initial POST fails with a 5xx.
 NEXUS_TRACING_MAX_RETRIES=3
 # Initial back-off delay between retries (e.g. 100ms, 1s).
 NEXUS_TRACING_RETRY_BASE_DELAY=100ms
 # Maximum back-off delay ceiling (e.g. 2s, 10s).
 NEXUS_TRACING_RETRY_MAX_DELAY=2s
 # Bounded channel capacity for the export queue (default: 256). A zero or
 # negative value is treated as the default.
 NEXUS_TRACING_QUEUE_SIZE=256
 # Batch size for OTLP trace exports (default: 64). Once reached, the
 # exporter flushes before draining more spans. Operators with high-
 # throughput/low-latency collectors may want larger batches; operators
 # with high-latency collectors may prefer smaller batches to reduce
 # per-batch loss exposure. Values < 1 fall back to the default.
 NEXUS_TRACING_BATCH_SIZE=64
 # Trace sampling probability in [0,1] (default: 1.0 = record everything).
 # Values <= 0 disable tracing entirely; values >= 1 record every trace.
 NEXUS_TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE=1.0
 
 # --- Local Ollama ---------------------------------------------------------
 NEXUS_OLLAMA_URL=http://localhost:11434
 NEXUS_ROUTER_MODEL=qwen3-coder:4b
 NEXUS_LOCAL_MODEL=qwen3-coder:8b
 NEXUS_EMBEDDING_MODEL=nomic-embed-text
 
 # --- Frontier API (OpenAI-compatible) ------------------------------------
 # Replace with a real key. When unset, frontier-bound requests will 401.
 NEXUS_FRONTIER_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions
 NEXUS_FRONTIER_MODEL=gpt-4o
 NEXUS_FRONTIER_API_KEY=
 # USD per 1k tokens charged against the frontier provider. Approximates
 # OpenAI gpt-4o (~$5/M input tokens). Used by the frontier provider
 # selector as a deterministic cost weight before the metrics store has
 # observed any traffic, and as the default for the cost-avoidance baseline
 # rate below.
 NEXUS_FRONTIER_COST_PER_1K=0.005
 # JSON array of frontier provider objects for the multi-provider
 # selector (issue #45). Each object needs "name", "url", "model",
 # optional "apiKey", and "costPer1K". Leave empty to fall back to
 # the legacy NEXUS_FRONTIER_* vars above.
 # Example: [{"name":"openai","url":"https://api.openai.com/v1","model":"gpt-4o","apiKey":"sk-...","costPer1K":0.005}]
 NEXUS_FRONTIER_PROVIDERS=
 
 # Comma-separated list of provider names for the multi-provider
 # registry (issue #45). For each name the proxy reads
 # NEXUS_<NAME>_URL, NEXUS_<NAME>_MODEL, NEXUS_<NAME>_API_KEY,
 # and NEXUS_<NAME>_COST_PER_1K. When set, this replaces the
 # legacy NEXUS_FRONTIER_* / NEXUS_ZAI_* vars.
 # Leave empty to use legacy mode.
 NEXUS_PROVIDERS=
 
 # --- Z.ai fallback (issue #14) ----------------------------------------
 # Optional second fallback in the local-route cascade (frontier is tried
 # first when its key is set). Leave NEXUS_ZAI_API_KEY empty to skip.
 NEXUS_ZAI_URL=https://api.z.ai/v1/chat/completions
 NEXUS_ZAI_MODEL=glm-4.6
 NEXUS_ZAI_API_KEY=
 # USD per 1k tokens charged against the z.ai provider. Approximates
 # glm-4.6 (~$2/M). Used by the frontier provider selector's cost weight.
 NEXUS_ZAI_COST_PER_1K=0.002
 
 # --- Inbound auth (issue #109) -------------------------------------------
 # When set, every non-exempt endpoint requires a matching Bearer
 # token in the Authorization header. /healthz and /metrics stay open
 # for K8s probes and Prometheus scrapers. /status is gated by
 # default (set NEXUS_STATUS_PUBLIC=true to expose it without auth).
 # Leave empty for no auth (development default).
 NEXUS_PROXY_API_KEY=
 # Expose /status without auth? Default false — the diagnostics
 # surface (frontier configured, judge enabled, VRAM state) is
 # reconnaissance-grade. Set to true only behind a reverse-proxy ACL.
 NEXUS_STATUS_PUBLIC=false
 # Readiness probe mode for /readyz (issue #302). "degraded" (default)
 # always returns 200 while surfacing the degraded flag; "strict"
 # returns 503 when Ollama is down. Unrecognised values fail boot.
 NEXUS_READINESS_MODE=degraded
 
 # --- Auth brute-force protection (issue #296) -------------------------
 # After NEXUS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_BURST auth failures from the same client IP
 # within the window, the proxy returns 429 with Retry-After. RPM
 # controls the steady-state failure-tracking rate. Set RPM <= 0 to
 # disable entirely (stock behaviour unchanged).
 NEXUS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_RPM=5
 NEXUS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_BURST=3
 # Sliding window for tracking failures (default 5 min).
 NEXUS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW=5m
 
 # --- TOON prompt compression (issue #123) ------------------------------
 # TOON rewrites JSON arrays-of-objects into a columnar text shape
 # (items[N]{k1,k2}: / indented value rows) to cut token usage on
 # data-heavy prompts. The fenced-block path (```json arrays) always
 # runs. NEXUS_TOON_UNFENCED adds a second pass that also compresses
 # bare `[ {...} ]` arrays pasted without a code fence and arrays
 # embedded in prose — only arrays of >=2 objects are rewritten so the
 # column header pays off. Set to false if a downstream parser depends
 # on raw JSON reaching the model.
 NEXUS_TOON_UNFENCED=true
 # Custom notice appended when TOON compression was applied.
 # Empty uses the built-in default notice; set to override or disable.
 NEXUS_TOON_NOTICE=
 
 # --- Cost-avoidance baseline (issue #73) -------------------------------
 # The baseline represents what each request WOULD have cost if sent to
 # the frontier provider, regardless of the actual route taken.
 # savings_usd = max(baseline_cost - actual_cost, 0). When provider /
 # model are empty they default to the configured frontier values, so a
 # stock deployment gets cost-avoidance tracking without extra config.
 # Provider name for the cost baseline (default: "frontier").
 NEXUS_COST_BASELINE_PROVIDER=frontier
 # Model name for the cost baseline (default: NEXUS_FRONTIER_MODEL).
 NEXUS_COST_BASELINE_MODEL=gpt-4o
 # USD per 1k tokens for baseline valuation (default: NEXUS_FRONTIER_COST_PER_1K).
 NEXUS_COST_BASELINE_RATE_PER_1K=0.005
 
 # --- Spend/budget guard + alerting (issue #183, #201) -------------------
 # Rolling 24h frontier spend cap in USD. When set, the proxy tracks
 # frontier API costs in a sliding 24h window and rejects new
 # frontier/fusion requests with HTTP 429 when the limit is exhausted.
 # Leave unset (or 0) to disable the budget guard entirely.
 NEXUS_BUDGET_DAILY_LIMIT=0
 # Enable alerting when spend approaches or hits the budget limit.
 # When true, the guard emits Prometheus counters and log messages
 # when the budget is exceeded and when spend crosses the threshold.
 NEXUS_BUDGET_ALERT_ENABLED=false
 # Fraction of the budget limit that triggers the "approaching" alert.
 # When spend >= threshold * limit, an alert is logged/emitted. Default 0.8.
 NEXUS_BUDGET_ALERT_THRESHOLD=0.8
 # Optional webhook URL for JSON alert payloads. When set, a POST is
 # sent to this URL with the alert details (exceeded/approaching).
 # The payload includes: event, spent_usd, limit_usd, remaining_usd.
 # Leave empty to disable webhook alerting.
 NEXUS_BUDGET_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL=
 
 # --- Frontier provider selector (issue #45) ----------------------------
 # When multiple frontier providers are registered (e.g. OpenAI + z.ai),
 # the selector picks the cheapest acceptable one based on observed
 # latency and the cost rates above. These knobs tune the look-back
 # window, the minimum observations before a provider is trusted, and
 # how often the pick is refreshed. Defaults match router.DefaultSelector*.
 # Look-back window for observed outcomes; older samples drop off.
 NEXUS_SELECTOR_WINDOW=1h
 # Observations a provider needs before its stats are trusted; below this
 # the selector stays neutral (keeps the current pick).
 NEXUS_SELECTOR_MIN_SAMPLES=5
 # How often the selector recomputes its pick. 0 recomputes on every call.
 NEXUS_SELECTOR_REFRESH=60s
 # P95 blend factor in [0,1] (issue #450). 0 keeps the legacy P50-only
 # scoring byte-for-byte; values > 0 penalise providers whose long-tail
 # (P95) latency substantially exceeds their steady-state (P50). At 1.0
 # the selector ranks purely by (P95 * cost). Values outside [0,1] fail
 # config validation at boot.
 NEXUS_PROVIDER_TAIL_WEIGHT=0.0
 
 # --- RAG ------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Directory of golden code snippets; auto-created if missing.
 NEXUS_EXAMPLES_DIR=./few_shot_examples
 # Cosine similarity threshold (0.0-1.0) above which a few-shot is injected.
 NEXUS_RAG_THRESHOLD=0.55
 # RAG embedder backend selector (issue #238). One of:
 #   ollama  — local Ollama /api/embeddings (default, needs NEXUS_OLLAMA_URL)
 #   openai  — OpenAI /v1/embeddings (needs NEXUS_FRONTIER_API_KEY set;
 #             model is NEXUS_EMBEDDING_MODEL, default text-embedding-3-small)
 #   cohere  — Cohere /v1/embed (needs NEXUS_COHERE_API_KEY set)
 NEXUS_EMBEDDER_TYPE=ollama
 # Base URL for openai/cohere embedder backends. Defaults are the public
 # provider endpoints; override when using a proxy or custom deployment.
 # Default: https://api.openai.com/v1 (openai), https://api.cohere.ai/v1
 # (cohere), or NEXUS_OLLAMA_URL (ollama).
 NEXUS_EMBEDDER_BASE_URL=
 # NEXUS_EMBEDDER_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1   # for openai
 # NEXUS_EMBEDDER_BASE_URL=https://api.cohere.ai/v1     # for cohere
 # Path to the SQLite database that caches precomputed few-shot embeddings
 # (issue #46). On boot the proxy reads from this DB instead of calling
 # Ollama /api/embeddings for every snippet — restart is O(rows), not
 # O(snippets * HTTP round-trip). A background watcher (next var)
 # incrementally picks up new / modified / deleted files in
 # NEXUS_EXAMPLES_DIR. Parent directories are created on demand. Set
 # to empty to fall back to the legacy in-memory-only path.
 NEXUS_RAG_DB=~/.cache/nexus-proxy/rag.db
 # Cadence for the background file watcher (issue #46). Set to 0 to
 # disable the watcher — boot-time load still works, but runtime
 # edits to NEXUS_EXAMPLES_DIR won't be picked up until restart.
 NEXUS_RAG_POLL_INTERVAL=30s
 # Bounded LRU cache for prompt embeddings (issue #115). Embeddings
 # are deterministic per model+text, so repeat prompts skip the
 # Ollama /api/embeddings round-trip entirely. Default 256 keeps
 # memory flat; set to 0 to disable caching.
 NEXUS_RAG_EMBED_CACHE_SIZE=256
 # Per-entry TTL for the prompt embedding cache. A TTL is required for
 # the cache to be active; 0 means pass-through (cache disabled even if
 # size > 0). Default 24h keeps entries alive across a typical working
 # day while still eventually evicting stale embeddings.
 NEXUS_RAG_EMBED_CACHE_TTL=24h
 # Max time a waiter goroutine waits for a concurrent in-flight Embed call
 # before giving up and falling through to a direct inner call (issue #800).
 # Default 5s; set to 0 to disable (waiters wait indefinitely).
 NEXUS_RAG_EMBED_CACHE_WAIT_TIMEOUT=5s
 # RAG circuit breaker (issue #222). After this many consecutive Ollama
 # /api/embeddings failures, the breaker trips and Embed returns
 # ErrCircuitOpen during the cooldown window. Set to 0 to disable the
 # circuit breaker entirely.
 NEXUS_RAG_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD=3
 # Cooldown duration after the RAG circuit breaker trips. During the
 # cooldown, Embed returns ErrCircuitOpen immediately without calling
 # Ollama. The breaker recloses on the first successful embed.
 NEXUS_RAG_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_COOLDOWN=30s
 # Batch size for RAG embedding (issue #771). When > 0, IndexDir batches
 # files in groups of this size and calls EmbedBatch to reduce HTTP
 # round-trips by ~60-80%. Set to 0 to disable batching.
 NEXUS_RAG_BATCH_SIZE=32
 # API key for Cohere embedder (when NEXUS_EMBEDDER_TYPE=cohere).
 NEXUS_COHERE_API_KEY=
 
 # --- Routing timeouts -----------------------------------------------------
 # Estimated tokens above this force-route to frontier (VRAM guardrail).
 NEXUS_TOKEN_GUARDRAIL=6000
 NEXUS_SLM_TIMEOUT=8s
 # SLM routing decision cache (issue #206). The SLM (qwen3-coder:4b)
 # makes routing decisions by calling Ollama /api/chat — ~200-1500 ms
 # per call. Decisions are near-deterministic (temperature 0.1), so
 # identical prompts hit the cache. Key is SHA256(prompt). LRU + TTL.
 # Max entries caps memory; set to 0 to disable the cache entirely.
 NEXUS_SLM_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=512
 # TTL for SLM routing decision cache entries. Set to 0 to disable expiry
 # (pure LRU eviction only). Default 30s keeps decisions fresh while
 # still absorbing bursts of identical prompts.
 NEXUS_SLM_CACHE_TTL=30s
 # Cosine similarity floor for semantic cache hits in the SLM decision
 # cache (issue #245). When > 0, prompts with similar intent but different
 # wording share cached route decisions. 0.0 disables semantic dedup
 # (exact SHA256 match only). Range [0.0-1.0]; out-of-range values
 # are clamped.
 NEXUS_SLMCACHE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD=0.0
 # Max stale entries before proactive eviction triggers in getSemantic
 # (issue #835). 0 disables proactive eviction (stale entries accumulate
 # silently until the next Set call); a positive value causes getSemantic
 # to spawn a background eviction goroutine when stale > maxStale.
 NEXUS_SLMCACHE_MAX_STALE=0
 # Hard-escalation threshold for SLM confidence (issue #301). When the
 # SLM returns local/fusion with confidence below this value, the
 # planner overrides to frontier. Default 0.3 is deliberately conservative:
 # it only fires when the SLM is quite uncertain, preserving local-route
 # savings for clear-cut cases. Set to 0 to disable the hard override
 # (soft bias via ConfidenceStore still applies when wired).
 NEXUS_SLM_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.3
 # DSL fast-pass patterns (issue #305). Comma-separated regexes that
 # bypass the SLM call for common, clearly-routed tasks. Unset vars
 # fall back to hardcoded defaults that preserve prior behaviour.
 # Simple formatting keywords that get a fast local-route pass.
 NEXUS_DSL_FORMATTING_PATTERNS=(?i)\b(css|format|docstring|lint|typo|boilerplate|debug|fix bug|git commit|sql query|parse json|validate input|regex|api endpoint|test|optimize|readme)\b
 # Architecture/system-design keywords that trigger fusion (run both
 # local and frontier in parallel, then arbitrate).
 NEXUS_DSL_FUSION_PATTERNS=(?i)\b(architectural design|system architecture)\b
 # Common coding task keywords that trigger a fast local-route pass.
 NEXUS_DSL_LOCAL_PATTERNS=(?i)\b(refactor|security scan|generate tests|explain this code|performance analysis)\b
 # Unicode-aware DSL patterns (issue #422). Matches non-ASCII text
 # categories like \p{Han} for Chinese. Empty means no Unicode fast-pass.
 NEXUS_DSL_UNICODE_PATTERNS=
 NEXUS_FUSION_TIMEOUT=120s
 
 # Per-attempt timeout for cascade fallback members (each retry gets this long).
 NEXUS_CASCADE_TIMEOUT=30s
 
 # Per-call timeout for the fusion arbiter synthesis step (issue #12).
 # Shorter than NEXUS_FUSION_TIMEOUT because the arbiter only does
 # synthesis — a slow arbiter must not pin the whole request indefinitely.
 NEXUS_ARBITER_TIMEOUT=60s
 # TTL for the fusion arbiter synthesis cache (issue #232, #773). When > 0,
 # arbiter responses are cached keyed by SHA-256 of (first.Content,
 # second.Content). Subsequent requests with identical panel-member
 # content return the cached synthesis without invoking the expensive
 # frontier arbiter call. Default 5m; set to 0 to disable entirely.
 NEXUS_ARBITER_CACHE_TTL=5m
 # Max entries cap for the arbiter synthesis cache (issue #773). When the
 # cap is reached, the least-recently-used entry is evicted. Default 512.
 NEXUS_ARBITER_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=512
 
 # --- Fusion progressive delivery (issue #48) --------------------------
 # When true (default), route=fusion streams the first panel member
 # to complete as a speculative OpenAI-compatible SSE chunk and only
 # invokes the arbiter when the second member disagrees (similarity
 # below NEXUS_FUSION_AGREEMENT_THRESHOLD). On agreement the user
 # sees the faster member's answer in ~max(local, frontier) time with
 # no arbiter cost. When false, the legacy blocking Panel is used:
 # both members fetched, arbiter always invoked — full backward compat.
 NEXUS_FUSION_PROGRESSIVE=true
 # Jaccard similarity [0.0-1.0] above which the two panel members are
 # considered to agree and the arbiter is skipped. Default 0.85 means
 # "skip when >=85% of tokens overlap". Out-of-range values are clamped
 # by upstream.PanelStreaming so a misconfigured operator cannot break
 # the path entirely (negative -> always skip, >1 -> only identical).
 NEXUS_FUSION_AGREEMENT_THRESHOLD=0.85
 
 # --- Ollama health poller (issue #8) ------------------------------------
 # Background poller that pings Ollama /api/tags and keeps a circuit
 # breaker. When the local Ollama is unreachable the chat handler
 # transparently reroutes RouteLocal to frontier (and skips the local
 # panel member of RouteFusion) and stamps X-Nexus-Degraded: true on
 # the response. Set NEXUS_HEALTH_POLL_INTERVAL to "0" to disable
 # polling entirely (the handler then assumes local is always healthy).
 NEXUS_HEALTH_POLL_INTERVAL=30s
 # Consecutive failed probes before the breaker trips and the local
 # route is treated as unhealthy. The breaker reopens on the next
 # successful probe.
 NEXUS_HEALTH_BREAKER_THRESHOLD=3
 # Per-probe HTTP timeout. Probes that exceed this count as failures.
 NEXUS_HEALTH_PROBE_TIMEOUT=5s
 
 # --- Hardware-aware VRAM probe (issue #6) -------------------------------
 # Background poller that samples free GPU VRAM (NVIDIA nvidia-smi or AMD
 # sysfs) and feeds the concurrency limiter below and the token guardrail.
 # Set NEXUS_PROBE_INTERVAL to "0" to disable periodic polling; the boot
 # probe still runs synchronously once. When the probe is disabled or
 # returns zero (no GPU / Ollama down), the chat handler falls back to
 # the static NEXUS_TOKEN_GUARDRAIL.
 # Polling cadence for the VRAM probe. 0 = boot snapshot only.
 NEXUS_PROBE_INTERVAL=60s
 # Per-probe command timeout; slower samples count as failures.
 NEXUS_PROBE_TIMEOUT=5s
 # Bytes-of-VRAM-per-token heuristic used to estimate safe headroom from
